title: A smooth projective scheme has an embeddable finite field model
statement: Let $F$ be a field of characteristic zero [def-weil-field] and let $X$ be a smooth projective $F$-scheme [def-pc-scheme], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-pc-projective-morphism], with projectivity meaning a closed immersion into some finite-dimensional projective space. There exist a subfield $k\subseteq F$ containing $\mathbf Q$ and generated by finitely many elements as a field over $\mathbf Q$, a smooth projective $k$-scheme $X_0$, an $F$-isomorphism $X_0\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}F\cong X$, and a field embedding $\sigma:k\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$. The scheme $X_{\sigma}=X_0\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k,\sigma}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf C$ is smooth projective over $\mathbf C$. Neither $X$ nor either model is required to be connected, nonempty, or geometrically integral.

source.place: Tags 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), 01ZP (lemma-descend-closed-immersion-finite-presentation), 0C0C (lemma-descend-smooth), applied to the directed union of finitely generated subfields of F. The complex embedding clause is the elementary transcendence-basis/algebraic-extension argument, expanded in report.md.

proof.text: Let $I$ be the set of finite subsets $A\subset F$, ordered by inclusion, and put $k_A=\mathbf Q(A)\subset F$. It is a nonempty directed set: $\varnothing$ is an index and $A\cup B$ bounds $A,B$. Each $k_A$ is generated by finitely many elements as a field. Their union is $F$, since $x\in k_{\{x\}}$ for every $x\in F$. The union is the ring colimit: compatible ring maps define a map on an element by choosing a stage containing it; common upper bounds prove independence and preservation of sums and products. The affine-limit clause of lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition therefore identifies $\operatorname{Spec}F$ with $\varprojlim_A\operatorname{Spec}k_A$. The stages are qcqs by lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs. Transitions are affine directly from the definition: a field spectrum has just one point, so its only opens are the whole spectrum and the empty scheme, with affine inverse images.

source.place: Tags 01YW, lemma-directed-inverse-system-affine-schemes-has-limit; 01ZM, lemma-descend-finite-presentation, application to the union of finitely generated subfields

proof.text: Choose a closed immersion $h:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_F$ from projectivity. Projective morphisms are proper by lem-pc-projective-proper, hence separated and of finite type by def-weil-proper-morphism; smoothness supplies local finite presentation. Thus $X\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is of finite presentation (locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated). The same holds for $\mathbf P^n_{k_A}\to\operatorname{Spec}k_A$: projective space is proper by lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper and thus of finite type and separated; pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth supplies local finite presentation. Its base is locally Noetherian because every ideal of a field is either $(0)$ or $(1)$, both finitely generated, and its spectrum itself is an affine cover. This verifies the definition of locally Noetherian, without a Noetherian assumption on $F$ beyond being a field.

source.place: Tag 01ZM hypotheses; projective properness and local finite presentation over a field

proof.text: Apply clause (1) of thm-pd-spreading-out to obtain a finitely presented $Y_A\to\operatorname{Spec}k_A$ and an $F$-isomorphism $Y_A\times_{k_A}F\cong X$. Projective-space base change identifies $\mathbf P^n_{k_A}\times_{k_A}F$ with $\mathbf P^n_F$. Apply clause (2) of thm-pd-spreading-out to $h$ under these identifications. After increasing $A$ (and replacing $Y_A$ by its base change to the larger stage), obtain a $k_A$-morphism $h_A:Y_A\to\mathbf P^n_{k_A}$, i.e. one compatible with the structural morphisms to $\operatorname{Spec}k_A$, whose base change to $F$ is exactly $h$. Finitely presented morphisms remain finitely presented under these base changes. The source $Y_A$ and target $\mathbf P^n_{k_A}$ are qcqs, since their structural morphisms are of finite presentation and their base is affine; this is clause (2) of lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence.

The map $h_A$ is locally of finite type. To check this at $y$, choose an affine target neighbourhood $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $h_A(y)$, then an affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}C\subseteq h_A^{-1}(V)$ of $y$ with $C$ finitely generated over $k_A$. Such a $U$ is obtained from a finite-type affine neighbourhood by taking a principal open inside $h_A^{-1}(V)$; adjoining the inverse of its defining element preserves finite generation. The same finite list of $k_A$-algebra generators of $C$ generates it as a $B$-algebra because $B\to C$ respects the $k_A$-structures. This is the affine-local definition of locally finite type.

source.place: Verification of the locally finite type hypothesis in Tag 01ZP, lemma-descend-closed-immersion-finite-presentation

proof.text: Apply lem-weil-pbc-descend-smooth-qcqs to the structural morphism $Y_A\to\operatorname{Spec}k_A$. Its limit pullback is the smooth morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}F$, so after increasing $A$ the structural morphism is smooth at every later stage. Fix such a stage $A'\supseteq A$ and let $h_{A'}$ be the base change of $h_A$ to $k_{A'}$, a $k_{A'}$-morphism $Y_{A'}\to\mathbf P^n_{k_{A'}}$. By clause (3) of lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence, $Y_{A'}$ and $\mathbf P^n_{k_{A'}}$ are of finite presentation over $k_{A'}$, so they are qcqs by its clause (2), and the argument of the preceding step, run at the stage $A'$, shows that $h_{A'}$ is locally of finite type. Its limit pullback is the chosen closed immersion $h$. Apply lem-weil-pbc-descend-closed-immersion to $h_{A'}$. Obtain a later stage $B$ with $h_B$ a closed immersion. Smoothness still holds at $B$. Set $k=k_B$ and $X_0=Y_B$. The closed immersion $h_B:X_0\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_k$ and quasi-compactness of its structural morphism show that $X_0$ is projective in the required convention. The base-change isomorphism $X_0\times_kF\cong X$ remains the one supplied by descent.

Write $k=\mathbf Q(b_1,\ldots,b_r)$ and put $E_j=\mathbf Q(b_1,\ldots,b_j)$. Inductively construct a countable field $E_j$ with an embedding $\tau_j:E_j\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$. For $j=0$, the rationals are countable, since each is represented by a pair of integers with nonzero denominator, and use their usual inclusion into $\mathbf C$. For the induction step apply lem-sfb-countable-simple-extension-embedding with $E=E_j$, $L=k$, $a=b_{j+1}$ and $\Omega=\mathbf C$. Its hypotheses hold: $E_j$ is countable by induction, $\mathbf C$ is algebraically closed by lem-weil-complex-algebraically-closed, and its cardinality is $2^{\aleph_0}>\aleph_0$ by lem-weil-complex-cardinality and Cantor's diagonal argument. It returns countability of $E_{j+1}$ and an embedding extending $\tau_j$. At $r$ this gives $\sigma:k\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$; when $r=0$ the base case already gives it.

source.place: Tag 09FZ, definition-generated-by, finite-generator induction; Tag 09G1, lemma-field-extension-generated-by-one-element, used through the supporting node

proof.text: Form $X_\sigma=X_0\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k,\sigma}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf C$. It is smooth by clause (2) of lem-pc-proper-base-change, and projective by lem-pc-projective-base-change. These are arbitrary base-change statements, so apply to the actual embedding $\sigma$ just constructed. None of the descent results or these base-change results requires a point, connectedness or geometric integrality of the schemes; the argument therefore includes the empty scheme and disconnected smooth projective schemes.
